title: Facebook createAdSet shows failure although the ad set was created
summary: Users saw native actions fail on `POST /Facebook/createAdSet` even though the ad set was created successfully on Meta. The immediate post-create read (`persistCreatedAdSet` → `getRawAdSet`) hit Meta's read-after-create inconsistency and returned 400, and that persistence error surfaced on the action response path.
symptoms: Native action createAdSet reported as broken/failed to the user
Meta Graph API 400: Unsupported get request. Object with ID does not exist, cannot be loaded due to missing permissions
warn: [Facebook] persistCreatedAdSet failed, pull will recover
No row in ClickHouse for the new traffic_source_item_id
root_cause: Meta's Graph API is not read-after-write consistent: an ad set created via `POST /adsets` (200) is not immediately readable via `GET /<id>` (400). `createAdSet` called `persistCreatedAdSet(created.id, action_id)` synchronously on the request path, so the failed follow-up read attached an error to the action log/response even though the create succeeded.
resolution_steps: Confirm the create actually succeeded: the trace shows `POST .../adsets` → 200 followed by `GET .../<id>` → 400 (Tempo trace for the action id).
Make `createAdSet` in `src/providers/native/Facebook/Facebook.ts` return success when the create call succeeds, regardless of immediate persistence outcome.
Decouple `persistCreatedAdSet` from the request path (fire-and-forget with a short retry/backoff) so post-create sync failures never surface on the action response.
Rely on the existing pull-based recovery (`pull will recover`) to backfill the ClickHouse row.
verification_steps: Create an ad set via the native action and confirm the action reports success.
Check the pod logs of ms-traffic-sources-v2-http for `persistCreatedAdSet` warnings — they may still appear but must not fail the action.
Confirm the ClickHouse row for the new traffic_source_item_id appears after the recovery pull.
